title: What If Every Dung Beetle Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every dung beetle vanished? Australia already found out what happens without them.
When cattle arrived, native beetles couldn't cope. A single cow drops 10 to 12 dung pads a day.
The dung sat there and smothered the grass. Nutrients washed into the rivers.
One big pad can breed up to three thousand bush flies in two weeks.
So from 1969, scientists brought in 53 species of beetle from Africa and Europe. 23 settled in.
Beetles bury the dung, and the pasture and the flies come under control. Without them, the barbecue would never be the same.

description:
